claims.text: Controlled support doping increases the oxide support's oxygen-vacancy density.
Increasing oxygen-vacancy density strengthens the electronic interaction between the oxide support and PGM clusters.
The higher concentration of surface oxygen vacancies enhances metal-support electronic coupling.
Oxygen vacancies in the support donate electrons to the PGM clusters.
Electron donation to the PGM clusters adjusts the adsorption energy of ethanol.
Electron donation to the PGM clusters adjusts the adsorption energies of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
The adjusted adsorption energies lower activation barriers for ethanol oxidation.
The adjusted adsorption energies stabilize transient reaction species.
The adjusted adsorption energies minimize catalyst poisoning.
Increasing oxygen-vacancy-mediated metal-support coupling improves ethanol-oxidation activity.
Increasing oxygen-vacancy-mediated metal-support coupling increases selectivity toward complete ethanol oxidation to CO2.
Reducing catalyst poisoning through modified adsorption enhances catalyst durability.
Catalysts on the doped supports will have higher ethanol-oxidation turnover frequencies than catalysts on untreated supports.
Catalysts on the doped supports will produce a larger fraction of complete oxidation products than catalysts on untreated supports.
Catalysts on the doped supports will exhibit greater electrochemical durability than catalysts on untreated supports.
The proposed effect is most prominent when electron transfer is rate limiting.
Mass-transport-limited conditions reduce the influence of enhanced metal-support coupling.
Very high or very low operating potentials reduce the influence of enhanced metal-support coupling.
